odc_type: incorrect time zone offset handling during DST transition
observation_summary: Setting fields like hour, minute, or second on a date-time object during a DST transition results in an unexpected change in the time zone offset.
reasoning_summary: The bug occurs because, during Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions, Joda-Time's date-time manipulation methods (like withHourOfDay, withMinuteOfHour, etc.) were not preserving the original time zone offset. When converting a local time back to UTC, the library was defaulting to a standard offset calculation rather than checking if the original offset should be maintained. The fix introduces a new method 'convertLocalToUTC' that accepts the original UTC instant, allowing the library to compare the original offset with the new one and retain the original offset if it remains valid, thus preventing unexpected shifts during DST overlaps.
